question: At Clover View Junior High, one half of the students go home on the school bus. One fourth go home by automobile. One tenth go home on their bicycles. The rest walk home. What fractional part of the students walk home?
solution:
All the students together represent \(1\). Since the walking students are the remaining group, subtract the bus, automobile, and bicycle fractions from \(1\). Using twentieths gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
1-\left(\frac12+\frac14+\frac1{10}\right)
&=\frac{20}{20}-\left(\frac{10}{20}+\frac5{20}+\frac2{20}\right)\\
&=\frac3{20}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore \(\frac3{20}\) of the students walk home, choice B.

edges.reason: Once denominators agree, the target adds or subtracts numerators in equal fractional units, directly using same-denominator arithmetic.

The general mixed-expression repertoire includes unlike-denominator addition/subtraction stages; these are scoped arithmetic components.
